task.name: spec check
task.start: Pointed at this file, you are told nothing else. This line is the first message of a new session, on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin; if your session holds anything before it beyond its own text, the repository's agent files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, rendered from specs/brief.xml) and its settings, stop, say so and build nothing. Your label is <model>-<effort> as the root's method model says. Read whole, in this order (root method read): every .rs file and every Cargo.toml under crates/, engines/ and tools/ as merged on main; specs/root.xml; specs/rules.xml; this file; then the files it names. Cut the branch SF-93-spec-check-v2-<model>-<effort> from the head of main. Every commit message starts with SF-93 and carries no attribution of any kind. Build what this file says, run its gates, push the branch and open the PR into main titled "SF-93 spec check v2 · <model>-<effort>" with the body the root's method pr lists. Show on the screen, as it happens, each step by its number and name, each test run with its result, and each gate. What this file, the root, the rules and the merged code do not say is a stop, not a guess.
task.piece: The spec check: a Rust crate, tools/specs, that reads specs/ and every owner's folder of the repository and prints every place they break the shape this file gives, one finding per line, exiting 1 when there is one and 0 when there is none. It checks the spec files; every owner's card, table files, rules, seeds and migrations; and that every owner's folder loads on PostgreSQL 18, its rules hold on an empty database, its seeds change nothing applied twice, and its versions give exactly its files. Its tests run it on the repository and, for every class of defect, plant one in a copy and prove the check names it. Nothing else: it changes no file of the repository and checks no Rust code.
task.before: Merged on main: the model, the engine interface and the MySQL engine (crates/model, crates/engine, engines/mysql); tools/architecture and tools/check.sh; specs/, the owners' folders (schema/cortex, schema/workspace, engines/mysql, engines/quill, docs/owner-template) with their owner.toml cards, as the design session that wrote this file merged them.
task.after: Every later task's file and every change to an owner's folder is checked by this crate before it is committed; tools/check.sh runs it through cargo test, and so needs Docker from this task on. The task postgres (t05) replaces the PostgreSQL image with the project's own programs.

file.quote: An open decision is a question no agent answers: it closes, in a design session, before the task it names in closes-before, and the spec check refuses that task's file while it is open.
Every quote in a spec is its file's own sentence, verbatim; the spec check refuses a quote its file does not hold.
so the table files always show the newest shape
the spec check (an engine table outside its engine's folder, or outside its engine's namespace)
A column a migration adds is written last

file.what: the method (schema, gates), the sequence (each task's id, key, name, file, builds) and the decisions (id, status, closes-before)
every rule's id, from, text and breach
the shape of an owner: its owner.toml, its table files, rules, migrations, and the two-version rename the check proves on PostgreSQL
the functions version 1 of the cortex creates before the rules

reads.crates: roxmltree for XML; toml for the owner cards; the standard library for the rest, PostgreSQL reached by running docker and its psql and pg_dump (std::process::Command). No other dependency.

command.form: cargo run -q -p schema-forge-specs [repository root], the root by default the repository the crate is in.
command.runs: Locally, with Docker running; it reads the repository, writes nothing in it, and removes the container it starts.

build.module: The crate schema-forge-specs, its [package.metadata.schema-forge] role = "tool", version, edition, publish, license and repository from the workspace; dependencies roxmltree and toml, each at an exact version.

module.public: pub fn check(root: &Path) -> Vec<Finding> (steps 1 to 12 and 14); pub fn load(root: &Path) -> Vec<Finding> (step 13); pub struct Finding { pub at: String, pub says: String } with Display as `<at>: <says>`; pub const POSTGRES_IMAGE: &str; nothing else is public
module.step: The spec files are specs/root.xml, specs/rules.xml, specs/lessons.xml, specs/brief.xml and every specs/tasks/*.xml, read in name order. Each must parse as XML; one that does not is `<path>: not XML: <the parser's message>` and is checked no further. The root element of specs/lessons.xml is lessons with product, version and date, and each lesson has id and date and exactly one found, one seen and one does, each with text; one lacking is `specs/lessons.xml: lesson <id> has no <element>`. The root element of specs/brief.xml is brief with product, version and date, holding welcome, agent-file, page-note, page-agent, intro, prompt, if-task-file, architecture, method, ways, wanted, start, read, database and helping, in that order, else `specs/brief.xml: <element> missing or out of order`; every group of read has a path, paths, or a source that is authority, sequence, guides or docs, else `specs/brief.xml: group <name> has no files`. Every specs/guides/*.xml has the root element guide with id (its file name without .xml), for, version and date, holding start, goal, boundaries, its phases numbered 1, 2, 3 in order, whole, stop and reference, else `<path>: <what is wrong>`.

The root element is root with the attributes product, version and date, and holds identity, authority, method, sequence and decisions, in that order; each one missing is `specs/root.xml: no <element>`. Every task of sequence has id (t followed by two digits), name and title (at most 80 characters); ids are unique; a key, when there is one, is SF- followed by digits and unique; a depends names a task id earlier in the sequence, else `specs/root.xml: task <id> depends on <value>, which is no earlier task`. A task with a file attribute names a file that exists, named specs/tasks/<key>.xml when the task has a key and specs/tasks/<id>-<name, spaces as hyphens>.xml when it has none, else `specs/root.xml: task <id> names <file>, which does not exist` or `specs/root.xml: task <id> names <file>, which is not its file name`; a task without one has text that starts with `Not written yet`, else `specs/root.xml: task <id> has no file and does not say it is not written yet`. Every decision has id, status (confirmed or open) and where or closes-before; a confirmed one has date; an open one has closes-before naming a task id of the sequence, else `specs/root.xml: decision <id> closes before <value>, which is no task`.

For every open decision, the task its closes-before names, and every task after it in the sequence, has no file attribute and no file under specs/tasks whose task element has its id; one that has is `<path>: task <id> is written while decision <decision> is open`.

The root element is rules with product, version and date; every rule has a unique id and exactly one from, one text and one breach, each with text; each lacking is `specs/rules.xml: rule <id> has no <element>`.

The root element is task with id, name, version and date; its children are, in this order, start, piece, before, after, reflects, reads, command, build, agent-decides, gates, owns, forbid, done (build holding tests); an element missing or out of order is `<path>: <element> missing or out of order`. Its id, name and key are a task of the root's sequence whose file attribute is this file's path, else `<path>: task <id> <name> is not the root's`. Its start holds `-v<version>-` and ` v<version> · ` of its version attribute, else `<path>: start does not carry version <version>`. Every step has n and name, the n numbering 1, 2, 3 within the file, else `<path>: steps not numbered in order`. Every prove of tests has a step attribute naming a step's n of the file, else `<path>: prove names step <value>, which is none`; the test names its items give by the root's method tests are distinct, else `<path>: two items give the test name <name>`. Every gate has id, kind (local, docker or ci), proves, at least one cmd and one expect, else `<path>: gate <id> lacks <what>`.

Every quote element whose nearest ancestor with a path attribute names a file holds text that is a substring of that file's text; when that ancestor names a folder, of the text of one file under it, its subfolders included. A quote that is not is `<path>: quote not in <file or folder>: <the quote's first 60 characters>`. An .xml file's text is its parsed text, every entity read (< as <); any other file's is its bytes as UTF-8. Whitespace in a quote and in the file compares as single spaces.

Every path attribute, and every word of a builds attribute, names a file or folder that exists, or one a builds attribute of a task of the root's sequence names (or that lies under one); <engine> in a path stands for every folder under engines/. One that does not is `<path>: names <value>, which does not exist`.

The owners are: the core owners schema/cortex and schema/workspace, each its own root; every engine, whose root is engines/<engine> and whose folder is engines/<engine>/schema; every feature, root features/<feature>, folder features/<feature>/schema; and the template, root docs/owner-template, folder docs/owner-template/schema, checked as an engine. Each root holds owner.toml with id, kind, namespace and version, and requires_cortex for an engine or a feature, else `<root>/owner.toml: no <key>`: id is a to z, 0 to 9 and _, and for an engine or a feature the name of its root (the template's is example); kind is core for the two core owners, engine under engines/ and docs/owner-template, feature under features/; namespace is the id for a core owner or a feature and engine_<id> for an engine; version is the greatest <n> of its migrations (step 12), 1 when there is none; requires_cortex is at least 1 and at most the cortex's version. Each breach is `<root>/owner.toml: <key> is <value>, not <what it must be>`.

Every .sql file directly in an owner's folder that holds a line starting `CREATE TABLE ` is a table file; any other .sql file there is enforce_rules.sql or grant_roles.sql of the cortex, or grants.sql of the workspace, else `<path>: neither a table file nor a file the method names`. A table file, its namespace the owner's: its first line is `-- <namespace>.<file name without .sql>: ` and a sentence; its header (the `--` lines before CREATE TABLE) holds `Owner: <id>.`; it holds exactly one CREATE TABLE, of `<namespace>.<file name without .sql>`, closed by a line `);`; besides it, only `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX <name> ON <its table>` statements and the COMMENT ON statements of its table. Every line of the table that starts a column definition (an identifier, quoted or not, then one of TEXT, INTEGER, BIGINT, NUMERIC, BOOLEAN, UUID, TIMESTAMPTZ and JSONB) carries a `--` comment of at least one word, else `<path>:<line>: column <name> has no comment`; a column of another type is `<path>:<line>: column <name> has the type <type>, which is none of the eight`. The table's primary key is one column, id, else `<path>: the primary key is not the one column id`. COMMENT ON TABLE holds the header's lines after the first's `<namespace>.<table>: ` and without `Owner: <id>.`, joined by single spaces, and there is one COMMENT ON COLUMN for each column, holding its line's comment, quotes doubled; one missing or different is `<path>: the database's comment on <table or column> is not its file's`. Every REFERENCES names a table qualified by a namespace: its own; or cortex, from any owner but the workspace; never another engine's or feature's, and the workspace only its own; else `<path>: refers to <table>, which is not its own or the cortex's`. No table or column name holds `__`.

Every file of an owner's rules/ folder is a rule: its first line is `-- <rule>: <sentence> Owner: <namespace>.` with <rule> its file name without .sql; it holds exactly one CREATE VIEW, of `<namespace>.broken_<rule, hyphens as underscores>`, whose query starts `SELECT '<rule>' AS rule, ` and names its second column id; and one COMMENT ON VIEW of that view holding the sentence. Each breach is `<path>: <what is wrong>`.

Every file of an owner's seeds/ folder holds only INSERT statements into a table of its own namespace, each ending `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;`, else `<path>: a seed writes only new rows of its own tables`.

The files of an owner's migrations/ folder are named <n>_<name>.sql, n numbering 2, 3, 4 with no gap, and, when there is one, 1_tables.sql beside them; else `<path>: migrations not numbered 1 to <n>`.

load(root) starts one container of POSTGRES_IMAGE (postgres:18-alpine pinned by its digest, sha256:0115267ab5a509022df9319c77be365cef335adb71556c75f60f5360ee247e71) with trust authentication, waits until it answers, works through docker exec psql and pg_dump, and removes the container whatever happens. It makes the roles sf_owner, sf_service and sf_reader, one database for the workspace and one for each engine and the template, each owned by sf_owner and each holding the cortex too, and applies to each, in one transaction and as sf_owner, every owner's version 1 as the root's method schema orders it: the namespace; the table files in the order of their foreign keys, ties by file name; for the cortex enforce_rules.sql and grant_roles.sql; the rules by file name; cortex.enforce_rules('<namespace>'); the seeds by file name; cortex.grant_roles('<namespace>'), or the workspace's grants.sql. A statement that fails is `<path>: does not load: <PostgreSQL's message>`. On the database so made: a foreign key whose target is not its target table's primary key is `<path>: refers to <table> by <columns>, which is not its primary key`; a rule view that lists a row is `<path>: rule <rule> lists rows of a new database`; the seeds applied again changing a row is `<path>: applying it again changes the database`. And for an owner with migrations, a second database with the cortex where its versions 1 to n are applied in order: the schema-only pg_dump of its namespace, its lines sorted, equal to the first database's, else `<owner>: its versions do not give its files: <the first line that differs>`. As sf_service, on each database: creating a table in each namespace is refused, else `<owner>: sf_service can change the schema`. Docker not running is the one finding `docker: not running: <its message>`.

specs/lock.xml lists every file of every owner's folder, every owner.toml, every file of docs/owner-template and postgres/manifest.toml, each with its SHA-256 as lowercase hex, and no other; a file whose bytes differ is `<path>: changed outside a design session`, a file locked and gone `<path>: locked, and gone`, a file not locked `<path>: not locked`.

build.module: Runs check and then load on the root given or the repository's, prints every finding by its Display, one per line, in the order found, then `spec check: <n> findings`, and exits 1 when n is not 0, else 0.

tests.how: tools/specs/tests/repository.rs runs check and load on the repository root itself and prints every finding on failure. Every other test, in tools/specs/tests/mutations.rs, copies specs/ and every owner's root of the repository into a temporary folder of its own (the file tree the check reads, nothing else), makes the one change its item names in the copy, runs check (or load, for the items of step 13) on the copy and asserts that a finding holds the text its item gives; the copy unchanged gives no finding. The items of step 13 and the repository's need Docker and are the gate Load; no test changes a file of the repository.
tests.prove: a spec file that is not XML is the finding not XML
a lesson without its does is the finding has no does
a brief group with no path, paths or source is the finding has no files
a guide whose phases skip a number is a finding naming the guide
a depends naming no earlier task is the finding which is no earlier task
a root without its decisions is the finding no decisions
a sequence task whose file is not named by its key is the finding which is not its file name
an open decision that closes before no task is the finding which is no task
a task file written while a decision that closes before it is open is the finding written while decision
a rule without its breach is the finding has no breach
a task file whose gates come before its build is the finding missing or out of order
a task file whose start carries another version is the finding does not carry version
a prove naming a step the file does not have is the finding which is none
a gate without an expect is the finding lacks
a quote changed by one word is the finding quote not in
a path attribute naming a missing file is the finding which does not exist
an engine whose card names another namespace, and a card whose version is not its migrations', are each a finding naming the key
a column line without its comment is the finding has no comment, naming the line
a column of a type none of the eight is the finding which is none of the eight
a table outside its owner's namespace, or not named as its file, is a finding naming the file
a database comment that differs from its column's comment is the finding is not its file's
an engine table referring to another engine's table is the finding which is not its own or the cortex's
a table whose primary key is not the one column id is the finding not the one column id
a rule whose view is not named broken and its rule is a finding naming the file
a seed that updates a row is the finding a seed writes only new rows
a migration numbered with a gap is the finding migrations not numbered
in Docker, a table file PostgreSQL refuses is the finding does not load, with PostgreSQL's message
in Docker, a rule that lists a row of a new database is the finding lists rows of a new database
in Docker, a seed whose rows take a new id each time it is applied is the finding changes the database
in Docker, the template with its last migration removed is the finding its versions do not give its files
in Docker, a role grant that lets sf_service create a table is the finding sf_service can change the schema
in Docker, the repository as merged gives no finding
a locked table file changed by one byte is the finding changed outside a design session
a table file added and not locked is the finding not locked

task.agent-decides: The names and the decomposition of the private functions and types inside tools/specs; how the files are walked and the SQL statements split within the steps; the container's name and how its readiness is awaited; the exact versions of roxmltree and toml (each the newest release at least two weeks old); the contents of the copies' changes within the items; the granularity of the commits. Nothing else: no finding text, no step, no public item, no image, no change to any file outside owns.

gates.note: Every gate runs from the repository root. A finding on the repository as merged is a stop, since this task may not change specs/ or an owner's folder.

gate.expect: the last line is `spec check: 0 findings` and the exit is 0

gate.proves: steps 1 to 14, each defect class named by the check
gate.expect: every test passes, one per item of the tests element, none ignored

gate.proves: the rest of the repository still passes, the architecture check among it
gate.expect: the last line is `== All checks passed`

task.forbid: specs/**; schema/**; engines/**; features/**; crates/**; docs/**; tools/architecture/**; tools/check.sh; tools/schema_comments.py.
task.done: tools/specs on the branch; every gate green and in the PR; nothing outside owns touched. After this task, cargo test and tools/check.sh refuse a spec file or an owner's folder that breaks the shape above or does not load on PostgreSQL 18 exactly as its versions say.
